**Conformal Kelly: Conformal Prediction Intervals as the Scale in Fractional Kelly Position Sizing** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01494)
- The paper proposes Conformal Kelly, a method combining conformal prediction intervals with fractional Kelly position sizing.
- The method achieves 28.5% annualized net log growth, with a Sharpe ratio of 1.34 and a 27.7% maximum drawdown.
- The S&P 500 is used as a benchmark, with a 15.9% annualized return.
- The method uses a 75% conformal interval, with a simple, unweighted, per-asset rolling quantile approach.

**Path Portfolio Optimization: Defect, Lift, and the Price of Path Complexity** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02355)
- The paper introduces a new framework for portfolio optimization, Path Portfolio Optimization.
- The framework builds on a path-first framework and asks whether it survives estimation.
- The method uses a linear functional of the signature, with the control living in a truncated tensor algebra.
- The covariance of signature coordinates is the non-group-like part of the expected signature, a defect form.

**Drawdown Risk Beyond Brownian Motion: A Monte-Carlo Framework, Non-Gaussian Extensions, and Long Memory** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00127)
- The paper develops a Monte-Carlo framework for drawdown risk beyond Brownian motion.
- The framework provides a more realistic approach to assessing drawdowns in systematic trading strategies.
- The method uses a transparent Monte-Carlo experiment, with validation against analytic benchmarks.
- The framework extends the mapping from drawdowns to four decision-relevant measures: maximum drawdown, maximum loss, final negative time, and longest recovery time.

**AI Financial Advice: Supply, Demand, and Life Cycle Implications** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01607)
- The paper examines the supply, demand, and life cycle implications of AI financial advice.
- The study finds that following AI advice would move respondents toward life cycle theory.
- The method uses a representative sample, with prompts seeking spending and investing advice from LLMs.
- The study finds that recommendations vary systematically by gender, prior AI experience, and financial literacy.

**Dynamic data generation and dynamic portfolio selection: an application of a score-based diffusion model** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09916)
- The paper applies a score-based diffusion model to dynamic data generation and dynamic portfolio selection.
- The method uses an adaptive score-based diffusion framework for dynamic data.
- The framework learns a generative model through conditional score matching and generates trajectories sequentially.
- The method outperforms several benchmarks, including the Markowitz portfolio, the equal-weight portfolio, and the S&P 500.

**Infinite Horizon Optimal Consumption: Intertemporal Hedging under Epstein-Zin Preferences** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02945)
- The paper studies infinite horizon optimal consumption under Epstein-Zin preferences.
- The method provides a variational characterization of the value function.
- The framework works in the regime θ∈(0,1), where there exists a unique generalized utility process.
- The study illustrates the scope of the framework with examples, including stochastic volatility and fat-tailed excess returns.

**CLQT: A Closed-Loop, Cost-Aware, Strategy-Consistent Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Portfolio-Management Agents** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29771)
- The paper introduces CLQT, a new benchmark for diagnostic evaluation of LLM portfolio-management agents.
- CLQT reframes closed-loop trading evaluation as diagnosis before ranking.
- The method uses a closed-loop, cost-aware, strategy-consistent, temporally-gated environment.
- The framework computes a five-axis capability scorecard (APM-CS: Coherence, Acuity, Composure, Discipline, Reliability).
